headline: Data centers drive AMD's third quarter
dek: Total revenue rose 45% and agentic AI is lifting its processors, per CNBC.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: Results beat estimates
body: AMD posted $13.38 billion in revenue, up 45%, per CNBC and SiliconANGLE.
The figure beat the analyst consensus of $13.09 billion (CNBC).

points.t: Agentic AI favors processors, says CNBC.
Rack-scale systems are used by big customers.

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: Outlook and contrast
body: AMD guides to about $17 billion for the fourth quarter, per CNBC.
PC and gaming chips fell 8% in the quarter, to $3.7 billion (CNBC).

items.t: Lisa Su expects strong growth with agents (CNBC).

caption.hook: AMD's revenue rose 45% in the third quarter, driven by data centers and agentic AI.
body: Per CNBC and SiliconANGLE, AMD posted $13.38 billion in revenue and data centers became 64% of the total. The company says its processors are growing again with agentic AI apps, which run well on CPUs.

The fourth-quarter outlook is about $17 billion, above what analysts expected. Anthropic, OpenAI, Microsoft, Oracle and Meta already use Helios systems. PC and gaming chips lost revenue, and the sector fears overspending on AI. Lisa Su says demand should grow strongly.
caption.cta: Will CPUs matter as much as GPUs in the agent era?
